articles.title: MAC commish Jon Steinbrecher: Replay officials instructed to use game feed of clock, not replay feed
articles.summary: MAC commissioner says correct protocol was not followed.
articles.body:
Mid-American Conference commissioner Jon Steinbrecher watched the final seconds of the Sept. 12 matchup between Western Michigan and Michigan at Michigan Stadium on television. Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood 's Hail Mary on the previous play sailed out of the end zone, and there was no time left on the clock viewers saw on the NBC television feed.

"I was certain that the play would be reviewed," Steinbrecher told The Sporting News. "From there, you're off to the races. You don't know what it's going to show."

Did anybody expect what happened next? Following an official review that put one second back on the clock, the Wolverines beat the Broncos 13-12 on Sept. 12 on a 47-yard Hail Mary pass from Underwood to JJ Buchanan . On Tuesday, the MAC submitted formal appeals to the FBS oversight committee and the College Football Playoff requesting that Western Michigan be recognized as the winner of the game.

"You're disappointed it's not being recorded as a 'W' right now," Steinbrecher said. "I think (Western Michigan) made a statement that people will remember."

Steinbrecher explained what was behind that decision to appeal in an interview with The Sporting News.

MAC commissioner discusses appeal of Western Michigan-Michigan

The MAC reversed its previous stance with a new statement that read:. "It is now evident that replay protocol was not followed in determining whether time remained on the game clock" at the end of the Michigan-Western Michigan game.

The statement says the Big Ten replay crew used the clock feed in its replay system – not the game clock displayed on NBC.

Is two separate clock feeds the major issue at hand for Steinbrecher?

"Correct," Steinbrecher said. "There is a protocol to be followed. We're instructed to utilize the game feed. Now, it's a unique situation here. I think the Big Ten may be the only one who is using a replay system that has a feed coming in that includes a clock in it so it has a clock within their replay system. That's kind of where we're at."

The MAC initially accepted the Big Ten's explanation for putting one second back on the clock after the game. Steinbrecher said the social media backlash did not make an impact on the MAC's decision to appeal.

"It was working the process," Steinbrecher said. "You take the information you have in the moment, and you make the best choices you can off that information. Then, you continue to seek and gather information to verify or refute where you're at. You continue to do that. Let's make sure this is buttoned up."

Steinbrecher continues to do work with Western Michigan school officials. On Tuesday, Western Michigan president Russ Kavalhuna released a statement that said : "We can respect the game while asking serious questions."

Steinbrecher said he admires how Western Michigan has handled the situation – including the players and coach Lance Taylor. The MAC commissioner also continues to have conversations with the Big Ten.

"I've had great conversations with the Big Ten and all that," Steinbrecher said." Everyone has been open on these things. I think there might just be a difference of opinion."

The Big Ten also released a statement Tuesday:

"The Big Ten stands by the statement released following the conclusion of the Western Michigan at Michigan game and the determination made by the replay officials. We will have no further comment on the matter."

Impact of MAC's appeal of Western Michigan-Michigan game

Steinbrecher – who took over as MAC commissioner in 2009 – has been on the winning side of a controversial Hail Mary finish against a Power 4 school. On Sept. 10, 2016, Central Michigan beat Oklahoma State 30-27 after a rule interpretation led to an extra down.

"I can almost guarantee that everybody — that most conferences — we've all had experiences when they've favored you and not favored you," Steinbrecher said.

On Tuesday, Michigan dropped out of the AP Top 25. The Wolverines received 69 votes. The Broncos received 12 votes. Steinbrecher said some new protocol questions must be answered in the aftermath of the Michigan-Western Michigan result regardless of the result of the appeal.

"That's part and parcel of all of this," Steinbrecher said. "Any time you have situations like that, we ought to be informed by them and let's learn from them and what processes, policies and procedures we can put in place to assist us if it would arise again."

That could entail a few tweaks — like adding tenths of a second to the game clock – but the issue at hands remains. There has to be one clock – not two – in the future.

"Would it be appropriate to put in tenths of seconds?" Steinbrecher asked. "We went through all that in the basketball world, right? We ultimately got there. I have no doubt we'll end up discussing that whether we'll get there or not. We clearly have to come to an agreement that all of us will use — if there are multiple feeds of clocks — what clock is being the ultimate arbiter? We've got to have agreement on that."

Dobbins | DEN @ KC 32) Jacory Croskey-Merritt | WAS @ PHI 33) Jordan Mason | MIN vs GB 34) Rachaad White | WAS @ PHI 35) Chuba Hubbard | CAR vs CHI 36) Tyler Allgeier | ARI @ LAC 37) Blake Corum | LAR vs SF 38) Chris Rodriguez Jr. | JAC vs CLE 39) Jonathon Brooks | CAR vs CHI 40) Kyle Monangai | CHI @ CAR 41) Aaron Jones Sr. | MIN vs GB 42) RJ Harvey | DEN @ KC 43) Keaton Mitchell | LAC vs ARI 44) Kaleb Johnson | PIT vs ATL 45) Dylan Sampson | CLE @ JAC 46) Sean Tucker | TB @ CIN 47) Tyrone Tracy Jr. | NYG vs DAL 48) Emanuel Wilson | SEA vs NE 49) Tyjae Spears | TEN vs NYJ 50) Samaje Perine | CIN vs TB

Which RBs Should You Start In Fantasy Football This Week?

Only time will tell you whether Robinson or Jahmyr Gibbs (or neither) was the right call at 1.01 this season, but there's little reason to think that Atlanta 's star can't shine in the season opener.

He logged 18+ touches in every September game last season and has hit that mark in seven of his past eight September appearances. That level of work feels like a forgone conclusion with Tyler Allgeier out of town and, once again, a lack of confidence in terms of the QB.

For his career, he's averaging 5.6 yards per touch and over 110 yards per game: give this man his touches and watch the box score light up. Gibbs was the only RB to score 20 PPR points against the Steelers last season, so maybe there's a slight matchup downgrade, but I'm not even sold on that (fifth most yards per carry allowed to running backs after contact inside the red zone last season).

We aren't 100% sure what to expect from this offense, but we know it'll all revolve around #7, and until we see the NFL consistently figure out a way to slow his efficiency, I'll be penciling him in for 100+ scrimmage yards with a better chance to find paydirt than to be held out of the paint (34 TDs in 51 career games).

This week should be fine by his lofty standards: Panthers, Packers , and Saints over the next three games could be downright dominant for the player I had atop my preseason rankings.

There's a lot to like here, but you didn't draft Corum with the thought that he'd be an asset from the jump. He averaged 5.1 YPC a season ago, and the best offense in the sport didn't hesitate to take Kyren Williams off the field for drives at a time to get him work.

Heck, he led the Rams in rushing in the NFC Title game against the Seahawks.

At cost, I thought he was the proper play in this backfield over the summer, and while I'm not budging off of that take, I'm not playing him until we have some 2026 data points.

The skill set limitations are a bit of a concern, especially if regression hits this offense as a whole. For his career, just 15 of his 216 touches have come through the air, and his next 15-yard reception at the professional level will be his first.

Your investment here was one with the long game in mind. Sit tight and be patient. I'm not sure he'll hit double digits in the touch department this week, and even if that is the case, nothing should change in how you view Corum: you're projecting growth as the season progresses and hoping that you can churn a profit when it matters most.

Here's a fun split for you to bring up at the Week 1 watch party when your friends ask you why you want to have the Jets/Titans on a TV.

Games decided by 3 or fewer points: 18.0 PPG

I like this game for one reason and one reason only: it's a chance to see the stars shine. It's going to be rare that either of these teams are in competitive games that allow for that to happen in an honest way, so yea, I'm excited to see what happens in this spot.

I haven't yet decided how to best do it (it hinges more on the lineup construction that I land on and you can see that in our FREE fantasy/betting newsletter that releases four times a week), but I'm going to have a skinny stack in this game with a player from both sides.

Hall is talented enough to be in consideration for that, though I currently project the Titans to win and thus am leaning in favor of their running game. Tennessee 's defense isn't bad, and in terms of yards allowed per carry before contact to running backs, they were actually the best in the sport (35.2% better than league average).

Hall can beat any defense with enough bites at the apple, and I expect that to be the case this weekend. I have him ranked as a RB1 for Sunday and already have him penciled in as a sell-high candidate.

It'll be easy. You sell your opposition on his raw talent and maybe even average offensive support. You get the highlight tape from this weekend and run it on a loop.

This is a player that has the potential to be a top-10 running back for the season from a talent perspective; that's not in question.

It's also not the question we are asking.

There are no points awarded for talent and if/when this offense becomes predictable due to game script (three straight games against the offensively charged NFC North certainly could cause that once we put a bow on Week 1), we are at risk of it being a coin flip if he's a viable RB2 (eight games last season as a top-24 option and eight outside of that).

Start him this week and sell him for a WR2 that you could see sustaining WR1 production next week.

articles.title: Jason Candle, UConn football team anticipate greater adversity as schedule toughens
articles.summary: From the weather to the final score, everything went the way of the UConn football team during its 56-7 demolition of Lafayette last Saturday, but the Huskie...
articles.body:
From the weather to the final score, everything went the way of the UConn football team during its 56-7 demolition of Lafayette last Saturday, but the Huskies aren't naïve enough to expect that outcome each week.

During his Week 2 press conference Monday, first-year UConn head coach Jason Candle was grateful to get his first win with his new program under his belt.

He praised the gameday environment at Pratt & Whitney Stadium at Rentschler Field in East Hartford and even described the playing surface as incredible.

With Maryland looming, however, Candle quickly changed his tune, noting that the competition is about to get much tougher.

He expects the Terrapins to be a strong challenge and provide the Huskies with something they didn't get in the opener.

"We haven't been through any adversity yet. That's the one thing that really stands out to me," Candle said. "What's going to happen and who are we when we get hit in the mouth? At some point in time throughout the course of the football season, that's going to happen."

This week, Candle expects UConn to focus on its practice details and habits to be ready to execute amid the chaos that Maryland, and future opponents, will bring to the field.

After Week 1's win over FCS Lafayette, Candle said the team has built some confidence and gotten through some first-time situations, ranging from practicing ahead of a game to staying at the hotel the night before a game.

"It's never real until you actually have to live it," he said.

On the field, the Huskies excelled, setting a program record with 671 total yards. Candle hopes the momentum can keep building moving forward.

"We were able to go out and have some success early in the game in all three phases and we should be able to build off some of the positives," Candle said. "Adversity is a great teacher, but so is success, right? You've just got to be smart enough and have enough humility to learn your lessons with both."

Candle explained that the football season is long and can take many paths, so it's important to come in every week with balanced emotions. He added that the responsibility for everyone is to continue improving.

"The minute we lose focus on that, we're probably losing the grip on who we want to be as people and certainly as a football team," Candle said.

Candle was most excited that dozens of players got to take the field last week, which builds repetition and communication.

He stressed that his team is not a final product; it should continue to evolve throughout the 12-game schedule.

"There's still potential to get better, and if there's not potential to get better, and there's not potential to grow and there's not potential for other guys to earn more opportunities, then we're just a finished product and sit here and play well the way we are for the next three months or sit here and die. It's what it is," Candle said.

UConn's new skipper added that he was proud of the cohesiveness displayed by his coaching staff last Saturday. He said the newly formed unit did fantastic.

"More importantly, the things that we didn't do a great job of on Saturday, we were able to sit in a room on Sunday and talk through and tell ourselves the truth," Candle said. "There's not an ego in here, where somebody isn't willing to go fix their mistakes for the greater good of the cause. If coaches can do that, if I can do that, then it's a much easier conversation with players."

UConn is next in action on Saturday at 3:30 vs. Maryland at Rentschler Field.

articles.title: NCAA can't overturn Michigan football win over Western Michigan despite protests
articles.summary: With the Mid-American Conference appealing Michigan football’s win over Western Michigan on Saturday, 13-12, which has been engulfed in controversy over cloc...
articles.body:
With the Mid-American Conference appealing Michigan football 's win over Western Michigan on Saturday, 13-12, which has been engulfed in controversy over clock management by the officiating crew, the NCAA has responded. While the Big Ten conference has doubled down on Michigan football 's win against Western Michigan, the NCAA has ended any hopes the Broncos had of getting a win.

As the MAC appealed the game, saying that the game should be changed in awarding Western Michigan the win, the NCAA ruled that there's no protocol for "overturning the outcome" of a contest, according to Ross Dellenger.

"The NCAA says that the association does not have a protocol for overturning the outcome of a game, and the FBS Oversight Committee does not have authority to overturn a game outcome," Dellenger wrote on X, formerly Twitter.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Why the MAC is appealing Michigan football's controversial win

This comes after the MAC was arguing that "replay protocol was not properly followed" in the contest at the end of the contest, and that Western Michigan should be "recognized as the winner."

"The MAC now says that 'replay protocol was not properly followed' in the Western Michigan-Michigan game and the league has filed a formal appeal with the NCAA FBS Oversight Committee to be recognized as the winner," Dellenger wrote on X.

Why the MAC feels this way stems from Saturday's game, with nine seconds left as the Broncos were up 12-7. Wolverines quarterback Bryce Underwood would attempt a Hail Mary, but it was incomplete with zero seconds left on the clock.

However, the referees ruled that a Western Michigan defender touched the ball out of bounds with one second left, leading to the second Hail Mary attempt and the miraculous JJ Buchanan catch for the walk-off win.

As the debate will be endless, the Wolverines look ahead to Week 2 against the University of Oklahoma on Saturday.

Week 1 fantasy football tight end decisions can get volatile quickly, especially at a position where a handful of targets or one red-zone look can swing an entire matchup. Our Week 1 TE rankings sort through the full starting landscape, from elite options like Brock Bowers and Trey McBride to more aggressive calls involving Colston Loveland, Tyler Warren, Travis Kelce, and Cade Otton. Which TEs Should You Start In Fantasy Football This Week?

I'm not a fan of Cardio Cade for our game. He's never cleared 600 yards in a season and has scored just 11 times across 63 career games. He's really only ever seen his number called when the WR room is limping along, and while that holds value in specific spots, I've always been of the belief that if the Bucs thought he was more than that, they'd give him the chance to be.

Maybe he sees north of five targets on a regular basis, and given the efficient nature of them, that's enough to slide him into the top-12 at the position on a reasonably consistent basis. It could happen, but I need to see it. This is a player with one game of 5+ receptions over the past 11 months, and the QB sneak stuff has yet to really be weaponized in a way that matters for us.

Keep an eye. If the route count is high and he adds some depth to his route tree, there will be a streaming situation where he makes sense or a DFS paydown strategy checks out. We could get there … I'm just not opening the season with that as my default setting.

22nd in PPR points last season among TEs

I say that to discount your excitement should he hang a decent number this week. Life without Mike Evans is going to take some getting used to, and given that this Bengals defense allowed a TE to crack double digits in terms of PPR points 14 times last season, Otton has a chance to return back-end TE1 numbers this week.

I still think he's nothing more than a streamer. A viable stream this week, sure, but don't get over your skis should he help you get a win in Week 1.

This game has a sleeper tight end in it that I don't like this week and a 2026 fade that I do.

The 2026 outlook for Okonkwo is largely positive. The target distribution behind Terry McLaurin is ambiguous at best, and his athletic profile works well with what this Jayden Daniels-led offense wants to do.

In his first game with the team, asking him to light the world on fire against a defense that was top-10 in both red zone trips allowed and the conversion of those trips into TDs is a bit much.

Give them four quarters to warm up to one another before diving in. Washington heads to Dallas next week, and I'll have Okonkwo ranked favorably relative to the rest of the industry barring disaster this weekend. As long as he's on the field with regularity against the Birds, it's a win for those of us who invested.

You can lose the Week 1 battle and win the 2026 war.

These strong offenses are going to burn you some weeks.

We see the Baltimore offense elevate the pass game or the run game. The Jags have four receivers that can have a big week and leave their teammates underachieving.

I think we see that at some level in Chicago, but Loveland should be immune to the duds, especially when you consider the low bar that it takes to be viable at the TE position.

Luther Burden, Rome Odunze, and D'Andre Swift are all players we like and drafted as weekly assets this summer. I think that was the right call, but if you're asking me which skill player leads the team in startable weeks, it's Loveland, and it's not close.

If you asked me which of them would lead them in Tier 1 weeks (define it however you'd like), it's Loveland.

I don't think he needs to be facing the Panthers (second most yards allowed per target to tight ends last season) to establish himself as the clear alpha in this offense, but it doesn't hurt. This is a great pay-up option in the DFS space: he's in the mix to lead the position in scoring when all is said and done this week.

articles.title: Despite a 4-year snub, Ronaldo still holds one major Ballon d'Or record Messi perhaps will never match
articles.summary: Football News: Despite being absent from the Ballon d'Or shortlist for four years, Cristiano Ronaldo still holds the record for the most nominations, exceeding Lionel Messi by one. This article explores their ongoing rivalry, Messi's latest nomination, and their respective achievements in football history.
articles.body: Cristiano Ronaldo may have missed the Ballon d'Or shortlist for a fourth consecutive year, but there is still one major category in the award's history where the Portugal star remains ahead of Lionel Messi.Messi's return to the 2026 shortlist has brought the two greatest rivals of their generation back into the same conversation, but it has not been enough to overturn Ronaldo's long-standing advantage for the most Ballon d'Or nominations.Ronaldo remains one nomination ahead of MessiFrance Football has revealed the final list of 30 nominees for the 2026 Ballon d'Or, with Messi included after another impressive campaign for club and country.His inclusion takes Messi's career total to 17 Ballon d'Or nominations, according to Spanish newspaper AS, leaving him second on the all-time list.Ronaldo remains out in front with 18 nominations.That is particularly notable given that Ronaldo has not appeared on the shortlist since 2022.Also read: Why Cristiano Ronaldo wasn’t nominated for the 2026 Ballon d’Or despite ending 7-year trophy droughtCristiano Ronaldo holds the all-time record with 18 Ballon d’Or nominations, with his first coming in 2004. He then appeared among the award’s initial contenders for 18 consecutive years, an extraordinary run that lasted until 2022.Out of those 18 nominations, he won the prestigious trophy five times across his career. His victory years and the clubs he represented include:2008: Won his first award while playing for Manchester United after capturing the Premier League and UEFA Champions League trophies.2013: Won with Real Madrid following a stellar individual calendar year scoring 69 goals.2014: Won back-to-back awards with Real Madrid after breaking the record for the most goals scored in a single Champions League campaign.2016: Won with Real Madrid after securing both the Champions League and the historic UEFA Euro 2016 title with Portugal.2017: Won his fifth trophy with Real Madrid, matching his rival's count at that specific point in their careers.Messi's 2026 nomination therefore narrows the gap to just one, but Ronaldo still holds the record for the most Ballon d'Or nominations in history.Paolo Maldini sits third with 13 nominations, while Johan Cruyff, Franz Beckenbauer and Karim Benzema have each been nominated 12 times.Just behind them are Zlatan Ibrahimović, Gianluigi Buffon, Zinedine Zidane, Michel Platini and Eusébio, all of whom made the shortlist 11 times.Ronaldo's 18 appearances and Messi's 17 therefore put them comfortably clear of every other player in the history of the award.Messi's World Cup heroics and MLS form both strengthened his caseMessi's latest nomination was also supported by another outstanding World Cup campaign with Argentina, marking his record sixth consecutive appearance at the tournament. He helped lead his country to the 2026 final, scoring eight goals and providing four assists during the competition.The campaign also saw Messi briefly become the all-time leading scorer in World Cup history with 21 goals, before being overtaken by Kylian Mbappé.Those numbers added another major international achievement to his résumé and helped explain why he returned to the Ballon d'Or shortlist at the age of 39.His club form backed up the international résumé too. In the 2026 MLS season with Inter Miami, Messi has recorded 18 goals and 10 assists in 20 appearances, continuing to produce at an elite level even as the club defends the MLS Cup title it won for the first time last season. Between a World Cup final run and a productive campaign in MLS, Messi's case for a 17th nomination was built on two fronts at once, not just one.Messi is now the oldest nominated player of the 21st centuryMessi's latest nomination also brought him another individual record.At 39 years old, he has become the oldest player to be nominated for the Ballon d'Or in the 21st century, surpassing Ronaldo's previous mark.Ronaldo was 37 when he was nominated in 2022.Messi's achievement is impressive, but it does not give him the all-time record. That still belongs to Stanley Matthews, the inaugural Ballon d'Or winner in 1956.Matthews was 41 years old when he claimed the prestigious prize and remains the oldest player ever to win it.Messi has the bigger trophy haulThere is, however, one very important area where Messi has turned the tables.While Ronaldo leads the nominations count, Messi has won the Ballon d'Or more times than anyone else.The Argentine has collected the prize eight times, winning in 2009, 2010, 2011, 2012, 2015, 2019, 2021 and 2023.Ronaldo has won it five times.That means Messi holds the all-time record for Ballon d'Or victories, while Ronaldo remains the record-holder for nominations.The distinction is a fitting reflection of just how consistently the two players competed at the highest level throughout their careers.Their rivalry has consequently produced different historical records: Messi has the greater number of trophies and is now the oldest nominee of the modern era, while Ronaldo still has the greater number of appearances among the nominees. And even after missing the shortlist for the fourth year running, Ronaldo's name remains at the top of that particular ranking.Also read: Why Cristiano Ronaldo wasn’t nominated for the 2026 Ballon d’Or despite ending 7-year trophy droughtFor now, Messi is the one closing the gap. With his 17th nomination confirmed for 2026, he is now just one appearance behind Ronaldo, leaving the Portuguese star's record within reach, even if Ronaldo is no longer adding to it himself. articles.body:
Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris reportedly will not join LSU's roster for the 2026 season.

ESPN's Pete Thamel reported Tuesday the Tigers added two other players to their roster, which brings the total to 105 players. That means the roster is locked for the remainder of the campaign, and Wright and Harris cannot be added despite the attention they drew as former NFL players who were looking to join the program.

According to On3's Pete Nakos , cornerback Aidan Anding and defensive end Gabriel Reliford are the players being added to the roster.

Ross Dellenger of Yahoo Sports provided an update to the situation:

This comes after the SEC filed an amended complaint against LSU and even scheduled a vote to decide whether to expel the program from the conference.

ESPN's Thamel, Mark Schlabach and Dan Murphy reported the SEC was "not expected to take such action, but the filing indicates the seriousness of the league as it attempts to affirm the legal right to enforce its own rules."

The SEC also released a statement that said, "The SEC and its member universities have the right to establish, through agreed-upon governance procedures, the rules under which they voluntarily compete and to expect those rules to be followed. A commitment to those rules, and to the core principles of the Southeastern Conference, is an essential element of SEC membership.

"Today's filing is necessary to defend that right and preserve the Conference's ability to govern competition among its members."

Wright was waived by the Cleveland Browns in August, while Harris was waived by the New Orleans Saints. While they both practiced with LSU leading up to Saturday's season opener against Clemson, they were not added to the roster for the game.

They argued eligibility rules changing and providing five years for players meant they should be allowed to return to the college game. A Louisiana judge granted a temporary restraining order and then a preliminary injunction opening the possibility to play this season.

However, the SEC filed a federal suit while the league's other schools all agreed commissioner Greg Sankey could issue penalties such as the suspension of a head coach for half a season and a fine of half the team's annual operating budget if they played former professionals.

While the back and forth between the program and its own conference has generated plenty of headlines, the absence of Wright and Harris from LSU's roster for Saturday's game didn't hold the Tigers back in their commanding win over Clemson.

LSU won 51-10 behind 309 yards and four scores on the ground. The dominant rushing attack overwhelmed Clemson, while LSU's defense shut down the visitors' offense for the majority of the game.

Next up for LSU is a home game against Louisiana Tech.

articles.title: NCAA Reportedly Establishes New Standard Timing Protocol After Michigan's Controversial Win Over WMU
articles.summary: The NCAA reportedly did not wait long to establish a new timing protocol in the aftermath of Michigan's controversial 13-12 victory over Western Michigan on Saturday.
articles.body:
The NCAA reportedly did not wait long to establish a new timing protocol in the aftermath of Michigan's controversial 13-12 victory over Western Michigan on Saturday.

ESPN's Jake Trotter reported Tuesday the new guidance will "establish a standard timing protocol that ensures consistency in the administration of all college football games."

A memo from NCAA national coordinator of officials Ron Snodgrass stated, "The official time for all college football games is the time displayed on the in-stadium game clock. When a replay review requires time to be restored or otherwise adjusted, the replay official's decision will be based on the embedded game clock contained within the program feed. If the broadcaster is unable to provide an embedded game clock, the replay official will use the game-clock graphic displayed as part of the broadcast feed.

Sark 'Shocked' by Michigan Field Storming

"This timing protocol should be followed consistently at all institutions and game sites."

Notably, Western Michigan would have come away with a stunning 12-7 upset victory over Michigan on Saturday had this protocol been in place.

After all, there was 0:00 showing on the NBC broadcast clock when Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood's first Hail Mary pass fell incomplete. Western Michigan players started to celebrate, but the officials put an extra second on the clock.

The Wolverines capitalized on their second chance, as Underwood's final heave fell into the hands of JJ Buchanan for a victory that sent the fans storming the field after a win over a MAC team.

It was controversial to say the least, but the Big Ten released a statement with a video replay that said Western Michigan defensive back Micah Davis started his leap from out of bounds and touched the ball with a second remaining.

"As shown in the provided video of what was viewed during the replay process, a side-by-side view of the play and the game clock, using a direct shot of the game clock in the stadium, was used to determine the final ruling," the statement said.

The story was once again in the headlines Tuesday when MAC commissioner Jon A. Steinbrecher requested the NCAA and the College Football Playoff selection committee overturn the result and recognize the Broncos as the "actual winner" of the contest.

"I recognize that the Oversight Committee does not ordinarily alter results recorded on the field," Steinbrecher wrote in a letter to the NCAA. "Nevertheless, the circumstances of this game are extraordinary. The final outcome was directly affected by a replay officiating error resulting from the failure to follow an established and specific protocol governing precisely this type of end-of-half timing situation."

However, Trotter noted the NCAA and the FBS oversight committee said they could not overturn the result of a game.

While Michigan escaped with a narrow one-point victory in its opener, things will get much more difficult in its next contest against Oklahoma. It also plays Ohio State, Oregon, Indiana, Penn State and Iowa later this season and will surely need to play much better than it did against Western Michigan to remain competitive.

The Wolverines dropped out of the Associated Press Top 25 on Tuesday.

articles.title: De la Fuente desvela lo que le dijo Trump y cataloga como "inaceptable" la trifulca de Argentina en el Mundial
articles.standfirst: Luis de la Fuente recordó la final del Mundial con Pablo Motos en el programa El Hormiguero
articles.summary: Luis de la Fuente recordó la final del Mundial con Pablo Motos en el programa El Hormiguero
articles.body: Luis de la Fuente, seleccionador de España, visitó el programa 'El Hormiguero' de Antena 3 para recordar sus experiencias tras ganar el Mundial 2026 y presentar su libro 'La vida se entrena cada día'. El técnico de 65 años le desveló a Pablo Motos lo que le dijo Donald Trump, presidente de Estados Unidos, cuando le entregó la copa de campeón del mundo. "Me dijo que merecía el Balón de Oro. Luego me dijo algo más, pero estoy en proceso con el inglés. Por si acaso, le contesté 'thank you very much' (muchas gracias)", contó el seleccionador español entre risas. Sobre la incidencia directa de Donald Trump en el Mundial, en la que intercedió con la FIFA para que le retirasen una tarjeta roja al estadounidense Balogun, apuntó que "el fútbol tiene que tomar sus decisiones propias, independientemente de lo que digan agentes externos. La FIFA no se debe dejar influir por nadie". Luis de la Fuente también habló sobre los incidentes al finalizar la final del Mundial protagonizados por los jugadores de la selección de Argentina. El seleccionador de España catalogó como "parte del fútbol" los roces durante el partido que acabó ganando España por 1-0: "Lo que pasó en el terreno de juego es normal. Yo jugué en los 80 y esa manera de ir fuerte es normal". "Si entrábamos en su juego, nos sacaría de nuestras condiciones. No por no tener ganas de bronca, sino porque queríamos demostrar que somos fieles a nuestro estilo", apuntó. De la Fuente se mostró más contundente con la actitud de algunos de los jugadores de la albiceleste al finalizar la final. "Lo que pasó al final del partido es inadmisible. Es inaceptable", sentenció a las hormigas 'Trancas y Barrancas'. El seleccionador de España cree que hay que cuidar la imagen del fútbol y que esto "no puede volver a suceder". La FIFA sancionó con 10 partidos a Leandro Paredes, el más salvaje de todos en ese tramo final, siete a Nahuel Molina, quien pegó a Rodri sin venir a cuento, otro a Almada, que sujetó a Gavi mientras le pegaba Leandro, tres a Ayala que soltó un puñetazo a Dani Olmo y otro a Gavi, el único a un jugador español, tras el empujón a Eric García, que también recibió un recado de Paredes.

articles.title: Al Madrid se le atraganta el gol
articles.standfirst: Los blancos lideran Europa en grandes ocasiones creadas (27), pero también en falladas (19); ante el Inter tuvieron una de sus menores posesiones en la Champions en las últimas décadas
articles.summary: Los blancos lideran Europa en grandes ocasiones creadas (27), pero también en falladas (19); ante el Inter tuvieron una de sus menores posesiones en la Champions en las últimas décadas
articles.body: El Real Madrid tiene un lujo y una condena en la misma jugada. Genera ocasiones a espuertas, pero las desperdicia con una facilidad poco característica de un equipo con su nivel pólvora. Lo que va de temporada refleja un estado halagüeño y alarmante a su vez. Los blancos encabezan el continente en grandes ocasiones creadas, con 27, y lo lideran también en el reverso de esa estadística: 19 falladas, la peor tasa de acierto de toda Europa. Dicho de otro modo, el Madrid perdona siete de cada diez balones claros que fabrica. Muy de cerca le sigue el Barcelona, con las mismas creadas y 15 erradas. El problema, además, se ha hecho costumbre en los dos últimos encuentros. Ante el Betis, en La Cartuja, el equipo firmó uno de esos partidos que se pierden contra toda lógica. Dominó, mereció y acumuló hasta tres goles esperados, con un penalti fallado por Mbappé incluido, para acabar cayendo sin premio. Ante el Inter, la película cambió de género pero no de moraleja. El estreno europeo fue un correcalles, un toma y daca abierto y cargado de ocasiones para ambos bandos, en el que el Madrid volvió a asomarse una y otra vez al gol sin la puntería necesaria para sentenciar. Si la noche acabó con los tres puntos en el bolsillo fue, en buena medida, gracias a un Courtois descomunal, autor de varias paradas de mérito que se erigieron en el verdadero seguro de vida del equipo. Sus primeros milagros a las órdenes de Mou. La receta de los goles llevó el sello inconfundible del trabajo del técnico luso. La presión alta funcionó a las mil maravillas en los primeros compases, y de ese acoso nacieron los dos tantos. Primero Mbappé, que persiguió la salida del Inter hasta forzar el error y culminar la asistencia de Brahim; después Valverde, que no dio por perdido un balón que el meta Josep Martínez creía dominado. Pero el guion volvió a torcerse por la vía de siempre. Con el partido de cara para dormirlo antes del descanso, el Madrid perdonó cuanto quiso y dejó vivo a un Inter que, lejos de rendirse, terminó asustando. El gol de Lautaro en el tramo final convirtió una velada que se vislumbraba plácida en un sufrimiento innecesario, pero también común en noches de Champions. Los números de posesión también exponen la realidad de este fenómeno. El 35,62% de balón que el Madrid tuvo ante el Inter lo sitúa entre los partidos con menos posesión del club en toda la Champions desde que existen registros de Opta. Exactemente en el octavo lugar. Por encima dominan varios duelos ante los Barça y los Bayern de Pep Guardiola. El registro más bajo de esa lista, un asfixiante 23,61% de posesión, lo firmó aquel Madrid del Clásico de 2010/11 que dirigía, precisamente, José Mourinho. Dieciséis años después, con el luso de nuevo en el banquillo, el equipo vuelve a abrazar esa misma renuncia al balón para golpear a la contra. Es parte de la identidad. El mourinhismo asume ese peaje de ceder el mando del juego a cambio de una pegada letal en la transición. El problema es que, de momento, esa pegada le está fallando en el último eslabón. El propio Mourinho, no obstante, dejó claro que este tipo de noches no son de su agrado, por mucho que terminen en final feliz. "Encuentro loco y una locura que no me gusta mucho", reconoció en rueda de prensa. "Me gusta más poder marcar cinco, seis o siete, pero teniendo un control absoluto y no necesitando la actuación de un portero absolutamente increíble". El luso, que prefiere ganar jugando mal a perder jugando bien, sabe de sobra que lo ideal es una tercera vía: ganar rematando lo que se genera.

articles.title: Barça - Feyenoord: Flick, a la tercera, ¿la vencida?
articles.standfirst: El técnico confía en lograr el torneo europeo en su tercera temporada en el banquillo culé
articles.summary: El técnico confía en lograr el torneo europeo en su tercera temporada en el banquillo culé
articles.body: El Barcelona arranca esta tarde su participación en la Champions League. Lo hace contra el Feyenoord del exazulgrana Giovanni van Bronckhorst en el Spotify Camp Nou. El torneo continental es la gran meta del Barça de Flick, que espera que a la tercera sea la vencida después de que viera el ambicioso objetivo frustrado en sus dos primeras temporadas en el banquillo culé, en las que levantó dos Ligas, dos Supercopas y una Copa del Rey. El Barcelona ansía conquistar este curso su sexta Champions League, tras las celebradas las campañas 14-15, 10-11, 08-09, 05-06 y 91-92. La Orejona se ha convertido casi en una obsesión. No sólo para Hansi Flick, que ya la levantó con el Bayern en la 19-20, también para los jugadores, Laporta y su Junta, la afición... El espectacular arranque de curso azulgrana invita, además, a los catalanes al optimismo. Han ganado los cuatro primeros encuentros de LaLiga con autoridad, en tres han firmado una manita; lideran la tabla en solitario; han marcado 17 goles y únicamente han encajado dos; Raphinha es Pichichi con seis tantos; todos sus futbolistas están ofreciendo su mejor versión y le complican al técnico la elección del once... En ese sentido, Flick apostará por una alineación muy competitiva en el que Raphinha, que ha marcado en los cuatro encuentros de LaLiga, volverá a liderar el ataque azulgrana. Todo apunta a que el técnico mantendrá el bloque que goleó al Valencia, con algunos retoques. Uno es obligado: Eric García es baja por sanción. Su lugar en el lateral derecho puede ser cubierto por Jules Koundé, Xavi Espart o Joao Cancelo. No se descarta tampoco que dé descanso a Fermín López y coloque a Dani Olmo en la mediapunta. Ambos están en un momento de forma excepcional. En cualquier caso, serían sólo retoques. Pero no sólo el gran arranque de curso culé invita al optimismo para este estreno de temporada continental. El Barça, eliminado la campaña pasada en cuartos de final por el Atlético, únicamente ha perdido en la jornada 1 en tres de sus 30 participaciones anteriores en la Champions League (21 victorias y seis empates) y el equipo catalán salió victorioso del único cruce entre ambas entidades. Fue en la segunda ronda de la Copa de Europa de la temporada 1974-75: tras un empate 0-0 en Rotterdam, el Barcelona ganó por 3-0 en el Spotify Camp Nou gracias a un hat-trick de Rexach. Además, hay un gran abismo en la trayectoria de ambas instituciones en la competición europea. Esta es la campaña número 31 del Barcelona en la fase principal de la Champions League, un récord de la competición que comparte con el Real Madrid: ha participado todas las temporadas desde la 2003/04. En cambio, esta es la octava participación del Feyenoord en la Champions League, y la tercera en cuatro temporadas. En su última intervención, en el curso 2024-25, se clasificó por primera vez para la fase eliminatoria, donde cayó ante el Inter en octavos de final. El conjunto de Van Bronckhorst afronta el cruce tras un buen inicio de curso: es tercero en la Eredivisie y su balance es de tres victorias, dos empates, 13 goles a favor y siete en contra. El exjugador azulgrana llega al partido, no obstante, con algunas bajas importantes por lesión, como las de Smal, Moder, Nieuwkoop y Bos. Y tiene la duda de Moussa.

articles.title: Valdano se 'Guardioliza' y hace reír a Raúl: "Mourinho sigue siendo el puto amo"
articles.standfirst: Jorge Valdano provocó la sonrisa de Raúl González Blanco al analizar el papel de Mourinho en las ruedas de prensa y su capacidad para trasladar mensajes
articles.summary: Jorge Valdano provocó la sonrisa de Raúl González Blanco al analizar el papel de Mourinho en las ruedas de prensa y su capacidad para trasladar mensajes
articles.body: Jorge Valdano, jugador del Real Madrid de 1984 a 1987 y entrenador del equipo merengue de 1994 a 1996, analizó 'Movistar Plus Deportes' la estrategia de Jose Mourinho en las ruedas de prensa en su segunda etapa en el Real Madrid. "En eso (las ruedas de prensa y comunicar) Mourinho sigue siendo el puto amo", dijo el exfutbolista de 70 años en 'La Casa del Fútbol'. Con esa frase Valdano parafraseó a Pep Guardiola y su legendario "Mourinho es el puto jefe y el puto amo en esta sala (la del Bernabéu)" de 2011. "En esta sala Mourinho es el puto jefe, el puto amo y no quiero competir en ningún instante. Sólo le recuerdo que hemos estado junto cuatro años. Me conoce y le conozco. Si se quiere quedar con los amigos de Florentino Pérez y la central lechera pero yo he trabajado cuatro años con él", dijo el entonces entrenador del Barcelona. Valdano destacó que "tiene 40 años de experiencia Mourinho y se le nota cuando está en las ruedas de prensa. Todo lo que dice son mensajes muy, muy bien orientados". "Se equivoca muy poco en ruedas de prensa y generalmente fortalece el vínculo con la afición, el vínculo con sus jugadores. Sabe perfectamente lo que defiende. En eso sigue siendo el puto amo", comentó Valdano sobre Mourinho, con el que coincidió en el Madrid la temporada 2010-2011 (el argentino como director deportivo y el luso como entrenador". El comentario de Valdano de Mourinho provocó la risa de Raúl González Blanco, que debutaba como comentarista de Movistar + y al que Mou le dedicó unas palabras mirando a cámara tras el triunfo del Real Madrid ante el Inter de Milán por 2-1. "Bien, ya tengo el titular", destacó Noemí de Miguel.

articles.title: Un portero de novena división que probó Guardiola en el Barcelona se convierte en Rey en Uganda
articles.standfirst: George Desmond Kamuras, guardameta de 36 años del Se Dons, ha sido elegido para ser rey del pueblo Tooro en Uganda
articles.summary: George Desmond Kamuras, guardameta de 36 años del Se Dons, ha sido elegido para ser rey del pueblo Tooro en Uganda
articles.body: La vida de George Desmond Kamurasi, un portero de la novena división de Inglaterra que en su adolescencia pasó por la cárcel, ha dado un vuelco descomunal. El guardameta de 36 años del Se Dons, un club de la Southern Counties East League Premier División, ha sido elegido rey por un comité de 21 miembros para convertirse en rey del pueblo Tooro en Uganda. El periodista ugandés Andrew Mwenda informó que en la votación del comité de sucesión del reino votaron 18 miembros y 15 se decantaron por Kamurasi. George Kamurasi nació en Inglaterra y es ciudadano británico, pero es el heredero de su primo Oyo Nyimba Kabamba Iguru Rukidi IV, que murió de cáncer con 34 años y fue el gobernante de esta comunidad ugandesa desde 1995, cuando apenas tenía tres años. George Desmond Kamurasi, que pertenece a la familia real Babiito, es hijo del príncipe George Desmond 'Jimmy” Mugeny' hermano menor del rey Patrick David Matthew Kaboyo Olimi, padre del propio Oyo, lo que convierte a Kamurasi y al monarca fallecido en primos hermanos. La familia del futbolista ha liderado la comunidad de Tooro durante mucho tiempo y, en 1954, su abuelo, el rey George Rukidi III, recibió a la reina Isabel II durante su visita a la nación africana. El portero del Se Dons, conocido como 'Big G', deberá decidir si continúa viviendo en Inglaterra o si se traslada a Uganda. En Uganda valoran el estilo y sin rodeos de George Kamurasi, mientras que otros cuestionan cómo un hombre criado en el Reino Unido puede representarlos. Infobae publica que George Desmond Kamurasi sufrió la muerte de su madre con 14 años, lo que le llevó a rodearse de malas compañías y a acabar en la cárcel. "Estaba enfadado. Tomé decisiones equivocadas. Me junté con malas compañías... En la cárcel me di cuenta de que todo lo que había hecho era culpa mía. Asumí mi responsabilidad", explicó el heredero el trono en 'Pulse Uganda'. El fútbol le sirvió a Kamurasi para abandonar la delincuencia: "Me descubrió la Academia Nike y terminé jugando en el F.C. Barcelona con Pep Guardiola observándome".

articles.body: Giuseppe Marotta: "Lautaro Martínez evitó cualquier tipo de negociación con el Barcelona" Giuseppe Marotta, presidente del Inter de Milán, habló sobre el frustrado interés del F.C. Barcelona en fichar a Lautaro Martínez. "El comportamiento de Lautaro Martínez fue ejemplar. Ha manifestado un grandísimo sentido de pertenencia para evitar cualquier tipo de negociación con el Barcelona", dijo Giuseppe Marotta en 'Sky Sports Italia' en la previa del partido de Champions League que el Inter acabó perdiendo 2-1 contra el Real Madrid. El dirigente nerazzurro aclaró que "los dos equipos tuvimos un acercamiento, pero no existían mínimamente las condiciones para abrir una negociación". "Lautaro representa la historia presente y futura de nuestro club. Para intentar ganar hay que tener también jugadores como él", subrayó Marotta. Lautaro Martínez: "Los rumores sobre el Barcelona eran ciertos" La semana pasada el propio Lautaro Martínez no eludió comentar los rumores de mercado que lo habían colocado en la órbita del Barcelona tras la caída del posible fichaje de Julián Álvarez por el cuadro culé. "Cuando llegan estas ofertas y estas llamadas, siempre es un placer, porque uno trabaja para mantenerse en la cima. Los rumores eran ciertos, pero tengo las ideas muy claras: he querido quedarme aquí con mis compañeros y con esta magnífica afición. Me quedaría para siempre y, mientras me quieran, me quedaré aquí. Pero en este trabajo ya lo sabemos: cuando ya no sirves, te echan. El Inter para mí es todo: orgullo, felicidad y ganas de seguir adelante. He vuelto a elegir quedarme aquí, quiero hacer grandes cosas en el Inter", dijo el delantero argentino en la 'Gran Gala del Calcio'. Lautaro Martínez tiene contrato con el Inter de Milán hasta 2029.

articles.summary: El guardameta del Real Oviedo solo ha encajado un gol en 360 minutos y suma tres porterías a cero en las cuatro primeras jornadas
articles.body: Aarón Escandell se ha convertido en una de las grandes certezas del Real Oviedo en el inicio de temporada. El guardameta ha disputado todos los minutos de las cuatro primeras jornadas y únicamente ha recogido una vez el balón de su portería. Granada, Albacete y Burgos se quedaron sin marcar ante los azules, mientras que Gharbi, con el Leganés, ha sido hasta el momento el único capaz de superarle. Los números respaldan su buen momento. Aarón acumula ocho paradas en 360 minutos, cinco de ellas ante remates realizados desde dentro del área, y presenta una media de apenas 0,25 goles encajados por encuentro. Tres porterías a cero en cuatro partidos que también reflejan la solidez defensiva que está consiguiendo construir Julián Calero en las primeras semanas de competición. Su última intervención decisiva llegó ante el Burgos. Con el Oviedo jugando con diez por la expulsión de Aldasoro, David González apareció en el segundo palo y remató prácticamente a bocajarro en el minuto 55, pero Aarón respondió con una gran parada. Una acción fundamental para mantener el 0-0 y permitir que posteriormente fueran los azules quienes incluso acariciasen la victoria. A sus 30 años, Aarón continúa siendo uno de los pilares de un Oviedo profundamente renovado este verano. Mientras Calero sigue buscando la mejor versión de su nuevo equipo, la portería ofrece pocas dudas; tres ceros en cuatro jornadas y un solo gol encajado.

articles.title: Dortmund bosses address Karetsas’ collapse against Villarreal
articles.summary: Borussia Dortmund’s 3-2 opening win over Villarreal in the Champions League on Tuesday was overshadowed by new signing Konstantinos Karetsas being carried of...
articles.body:
Borussia Dortmund 's 3-2 opening win over Villarreal in the Champions League on Tuesday was overshadowed by new signing Konstantinos Karetsas being carried off on a stretcher towards the end of the first half.

After the Black and Yellows initially announced that the Greek youngster had to come off due to circulatory problems, managing director for sport Lars Ricken and sporting director Ole Book shed some light on the incident and the player's condition.

"It was a circulatory problem that came completely out of nowhere. There had been no indication that anything was wrong," Ricken said in a post-match interview, admitting he was "quite shocked" by the incident.

Book was there himself and witnessed the incident up close.

"I went off with him, but at that moment he wasn't really able to speak. Obviously, we hope he gets better very, very quickly and that it's nothing serious," he said of the incident, which came "very suddenly".

"He sat down and was then taken to hospital for further examinations, where he still is now. That obviously puts a significant damper on the mood," he added.

Head coach Niko Kovac said he passed on the information that "everything was okay" to the rest of the team because they were "obviously worried too".

Ricken was impressed with how the other players handled the rest of the game given the shock.

"You have to give the team credit; it's not easy at all when a teammate is carried off on a stretcher and you don't know exactly what's wrong with him. You could sense that to some extent among the team and the fans."

articles.title: Chelsea: Where Estevao Willian fits in all-star attack
articles.summary: A look at where Estevao Willian could feature for Chelsea this season after the reminder of his quality in his cameo against Arsenal.
articles.body:
A late flourish from Estevao Willian almost snatched Chelsea a draw at Arsenal on Sunday.

His curling strike was saved by goalkeeper David Raya to preserve Arsenal 's lead, but it served as a reminder of the important role the 19-year-old Brazil winger could play in Xabi Alonso's side.

His game time has been limited so far this season by the club record £117m signing of Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa as well as the form of Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro.

The £51m signing from Brazilian club Palmeiras has played only 96 minutes this season, with 80 of those coming against League One side Luton Town in the Carabao Cup.

His remaining 16 minutes were in substitute appearances against Fulham and Premier League champions Arsenal , while he was unused as Chelsea held on for a narrow victory over Brighton in their third match of the campaign.

Reports in Brazil have suggested Estevao is unhappy with his lack of opportunities.

However, those claims have been denied by sources at Stamford Bridge and by people close to the player, some of whom have also expressed excitement about Chelsea 's summer recruitment - including the arrival of Rogers.

Chelsea regard Estevao as one of a small group of untouchable players that includes Palmer, Joao Pedro and Moises Caicedo.

The club have no intention of selling any of them, with Estevao central to the long-term planning of Alonso and Chelsea 's leadership team.

There were also early discussions over a new contract, with Chelsea keen to reward key players with improved terms in the coming months, having done so for Joao Pedro.

Asked whether Estevao's lack of involvement meant he was unhappy, Alonso replied: "No, Este is ready, training well. The other day he had a great impact.

"He is fully involved with a very good attitude every day. I count on Este 100% because of his potential. He is so young but he is learning and adapting quickly. The season is long."

Estevao also suffered a serious grade-four hamstring tear late last season and missed the World Cup, so is expected to build his involvement through the campaign.

Chelsea explored move for Fulham midfielder Berge

Two right-backs in midfield - are Chelsea short despite £349m spent?

Estevao came on for Pedro Neto, who has been operating as a wing-back in Alonso's new system, as Chelsea chased an equaliser on Sunday.

It is difficult to imagine any other in-game circumstance in which Estevao would be asked to perform the same role, given the defensive and physical demands placed on players in that position.

Instead, Palmer occupies Estevao's preferred inside-right number 10 role.

Estevao and Palmer have shown encouraging signs when used together when Alonso has played a back four - but he has deployed that shape only against Luton Town in the Carabao Cup.

Displacing Palmer for league games could prove difficult as Alonso regards him as both a dressing-room leader and one of his key attacking threats.

Alonso has also fielded close to his strongest side even in the Carabao Cup, with Chelsea not involved in European competition and with the new head coach eager to establish his tactical principles as quickly as possible following his arrival.

Estevao is not alone in struggling for meaningful minutes early in the season and, should Leeds United win at Stamford Bridge in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday, the Blues will have no further cup fixtures until the FA Cup in January.

That quietly makes Wednesday's game an important one in terms of keeping a 27-man squad satisfied.

Quenda, Emegha and Gittens are also hungry for more

Some of Chelsea 's other young attackers have also struggled to start matches, with Palmer and Rogers beginning every game.

Joao Pedro has started all three league matches, while experienced striker Danny Welbeck led the line against Luton. That has limited Emmanuel Emegha, who joined from Strasbourg in the summer, to only one appearance on the bench.

Similarly, defender Aaron Anselmino is also yet to play and was only included in one squad, albeit both players are managing fitness issues.

Other attacking options, including Geovany Quenda and Jamie Gittens, have featured for only eight and 10 minutes respectively across Chelsea 's four matches this season.

Quenda, who was signed despite interest from Manchester United in 2024, has also been left out of two of Alonso's matchday squads.

The situation might be even more challenging if it not for fitness issues affecting Moises Caicedo and Jordan Henderson, which have at times left Chelsea short in midfield.

Even then, summer signing Valentin Barco has been restricted to one start and a substitute appearance, as right-back Malo Gusto has started in midfield instead. Wing-back Marco Palestra also remains out injured.

If Chelsea had a fully fit squad available, they would have to leave six outfield players out of their matchday squad, with clubs permitted to name 11 starters and nine substitutes in English football.

Analysis of successful teams playing without European football suggests managers often rely on a relatively small core group of players.

Leicester City's surprise Premier League title-winning side of 2015-16 was achieved with only 14 players making more than 15 appearances in all competitions under Claudio Ranieri.

The following season, Chelsea won the title under Antonio Conte without European commitments. Only 13 players accumulated more than 1,500 minutes in all competitions.

While clubs are now allowed to make five substitutions, only 14 Newcastle United players exceeded the 1,500-minute mark when they qualified for the Champions League in 2022-23.

Perhaps the most relevant comparison is Manchester United after they finished third last season without European football. Only 13 players recorded more than 1,500 minutes across all competitions, although they exited both domestic cup competitions at an early stage.

For those on the fringes, including Estevao, a prolonged cup run could aide their chances of turning brief cameos into opportunities that Alonso cannot ignore.

articles.title: Raúl Varela: "La luna de miel del Real Madrid, los jugadores y Mourinho ya ha concluido"
articles.standfirst: El presentador de La Tribu analiza los pitos del Bernabéu ante el Inter y advierte del "panorama preocupante" que dejó el conjunto blanco pese a la victoria
articles.summary: El presentador de La Tribu analiza los pitos del Bernabéu ante el Inter y advierte del "panorama preocupante" que dejó el conjunto blanco pese a la victoria
articles.body: La victoria del Real Madrid ante el Inter no evitó el descontento del Santiago Bernabéu. Los pitos y el runrún durante el encuentro fueron el primer aviso para el equipo de José Mourinho, según el análisis de Raúl Varela en La Tribu. Varela recurrió a una frase de Pedro Riesco para explicar lo sucedido: "La luna de miel del Madrid, los jugadores y Mourinho ya ha concluido. No se si antes de lo previsto, pero parece claro que los pitos y el runrún constante durante un partido ante un Inter menor que concluyó 2-1 pero que pudo haber acabado 5-2 ó 3-4 son ese primer aviso taurino antesala de la devolución a corrales". El director de La Tribu puso el foco en una de las decisiones de Mourinho. "La noche ya comenzaba torcida por ese invento obligado por las tarjetas de ubicar a Trent Alexander Arnold en una posición en la que apenas sumó nada. Le dieron las gracias y una fotografía de recuerdo porque difícilmente volverá a repetir como centrocampista", señaló. El Inter encontró facilidades desde el comienzo y obligó a aparecer a Courtois. "Los neroazurris campaban a sus anchas y desde el primer minuto consiguieron que Courtois fuese lo mejor de la noche. Ahí sí que estamos de acuerdo con Mou. El que premió a Valverde estaba viendo a De la Fuente en El Hormiguero", afirmó Varela. Mbappé sí volvió a encontrarse con el gol: "Mbappé marcó pronto y esbozó una sonrisa pícara como diciendo 'os lo dije ayer y no me creíais'". Varela destacó además que "los dos goles del Madrid, con regalos defensivos gruesos incluidos vinieron precedidos de ese trabajo de presión, de esa carrerita de más". En ese punto apareció también la comparación con Lamine Yamal y la carrera por el Balón de Oro. "Lamine Yamal, listo donde los haya, ya advirtió que él sí dará desde Barcelona" esa carrerita de más "para posicionarse en la acera contraria en el relato de cómo deben comportarse los aspirantes al Balón de Oro, uno por cierto reivindicándolo para sí mismo y el otro, astuto, dejándolo en manos de los que preguntamos", explicó. Más allá del resultado, Varela incidió en las sensaciones que dejó el equipo. "El desorden, la falta de intensidad, no la de Vinicius, el más pitado aún después de batir su récord de recuperaciones con doce balones arrebatados a los italianos, y la falta de respuestas desde el banquillo dejaron un panorama preocupante", aseguró. Una actuación que, a juicio de Varela, recordó a problemas que el Real Madrid ya había mostrado anteriormente: "No parece el Inter de Chivu que ocupe lugar en el primer escalón de esta Champions que no ha hecho sino comenzar pero que tampoco parece haber espantado los defectos que en las dos últimas temporadas condenaron al plantel". Para cerrar su análisis, Varela utilizó una comparación para describir el rápido cambio de escenario: "Lo de ayer me recuerda a ese chiste malo que dice: al principio mi matrimonio era todo pasión, todo amor. Luego, al salir de la Iglesia, se estropeó todo". Y terminó con un mensaje para Mourinho después del primer aviso del Bernabéu: "Pues eso, que toca penitencia, asunción de los pecados y propósito de enmienda. Catequesis para Mou".

articles.title: Huijsen talks Mourinho, Mbappe, Courtois, Konate after Real Madrid 2-1 Inter Milan: ‘We could have won 5-0 or 6-1’
articles.summary: Dean Huijsen has revealed that Jose Mourinho is demanding more from him after the Real Madrid defender played another important role in the 2-1 Champions Lea...
articles.body:
Dean Huijsen has revealed that Jose Mourinho is demanding more from him after the Real Madrid defender played another important role in the 2-1 Champions League victory over Inter Milan .

Huijsen has established himself in the heart of Madrid's defence this season, but the 21-year-old insists his strong start means little unless he can maintain that level throughout the campaign.

He also credited Mourinho for challenging him to reach another level.

"I think he's really on my case. He pushes me hard, and that's good because he knows what I'm capable of.

"He helps me a lot and I'm happy. He pushes me so that I can improve and take that step forward," he said.

Despite becoming an increasingly important part of Real Madrid's defence, Huijsen was keen to keep his early-season form in perspective.

"We have to keep it up. Five matches are nothing; we need to have a good season as a whole."

The defender was also pleased with the victory over Inter but felt Madrid should have put the contest beyond doubt much earlier.

Dean Huijsen has revealed how Mourinho is backing him. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images)

"They're a great team and have reached the Champions League final in each of the last two years. We have to keep it up; it's the three points that count.

"I think we played a good match. If we'd managed to make it 3–0, it would have been over there and then," he said.

Huijsen again highlighted Madrid's missed chances when asked about Thibaut Courtois ' performance.

"It was a mad match, but if we'd made it 3–0… I think we had one at the end of the first half and quite a few in the second.

"If we'd managed to score them, we could have won 5–0 or 6–1," he noted.

He also backed Kylian Mbappe 's Ballon d'Or prospects, stating

"I don't know, I'm not one of those who votes. I think he's in with a very good chance. We know the quality he possesses.

Huijsen has nothing but praise for Ibrahima Konate . (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images)

"He's a very special player and I hope he continues to score plenty of goals for us," he said.

Mourinho's demand for greater competitiveness was another theme of Huijsen's assessment.

"I think we need to be a bit more competitive; that's what the manager said.

"At the end of the day, football is also about emotions and you have to be more competitive," he explained.

Huijsen also praised his centre-back partner Ibrahima Konate by concluding

"He's a force to be reckoned with. He's excellent in defence and on the ball too.

"He's strong, tall and doesn't shy away from a challenge. We get on well together."
